newsitem.title: FRANCE: France puts positive spin on Algerian vote report.
newsitem.headline: France puts positive spin on Algerian vote report.

text.p: France said on Monday it took note of a United Nations report critical of the conduct of parts of Algeria's general election but that Paris mainly saw in the vote a rejection of violence by the Algerian people.
"The French government has taken note of the report" which shed light on some irregularities, foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

"But whatever the case, in our eyes, this vote and the electoral campaign allowed the Algerian people to once again express their rejection of violence, attachment to peace and hope for a true political solution among Algerians," he said.

The report, by United Nations observers about the general election in which pro-government parties swept to a majority in the new parliament, said some observers had problems moving freely and there were questions over voting by security forces and at mobile polling stations.
Rummelhardt said the U.N. report report was written in a constructive spirit and contained positive as well as negative points.
"No major incident took place during the vote and we are grateful for this. France has noted the results and will not comment upon them as is our habit," he said.
